statement: The Omo I fossil (Omo Kibish, Ethiopia) was originally dated to 195 ± 5 thousand years ago via argon-argon dating of bracketing volcanic tuffs (McDougall, Brown & Fleagle 2005); a 2022 study using geochemical fingerprinting of an overlying volcanic ash layer revised this to a minimum age of greater than 233,000 ± 22,000 years, since the ash constrains only a lower bound and the true age could be older.

sources.citation: McDougall, I., Brown, F.H., Fleagle, J.G. "Stratigraphic placement and age of modern humans from Kibish, Ethiopia." Nature 433: 733-736.
sources.author: McDougall et al.

sources.citation: Vidal, C.M., Lane, C.S., Asrat, A., et al. "Age of the oldest known Homo sapiens from eastern Africa." Nature 601: 579-583. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-04275-8
sources.author: Vidal et al.

notes: Complementary to, not competing with, the Jebel Irhoud dating: Jebel Irhoud remains older and shows more archaic cranial morphology; Omo I is younger and morphologically closer to fully modern humans.
